title: Counting sort execution and output
statement: Let $P$ be a program, let $q,d$ be natural numbers, and let the machine limits have word bound $W$, space bound $S$, and depth bound $D$. Let $A$ specify an item count $n$, source and destination addresses, a key address with stride and offset, a number $b$ of buckets, and a counter-array address. Suppose the routine at position $q$ in $P$ is the counting-sort routine; $S\leq W$; the source, destination, and counter intervals of lengths $n,n,b+1$ lie within the space bound and are pairwise disjoint; and the initial memory stores item $\mathrm{it}(i)$ at each source address for $i<n$. For each $i<n$, suppose the key address computed from $\mathrm{it}(i)$ lies within space, stores the value $kf(i)$, and $kf(i)<b$; moreover, each such key address lies outside both the destination and counter intervals. Then on the listed arguments and initial memory $\mu$, the routine has an execution at depth $d$ with cost at most $68n+58b+52$. Its final memory $\mu'$ places item $\mathrm{it}(j)$ at destination address $\mathrm{dst}+\mathrm{sortPos}(kf,n,j)$ for every $j<n$, stores at counter address $\mathrm{cnt}+t$ the number of indices $i<n$ with $kf(i)<t$ for every $t\leq b$, and agrees with $\mu$ outside the destination and counter intervals.
